title: forge.ParseRepo accepts non-GitHub hosts, so a GitLab origin passes the close-out guess and fails only at REST time
body: ParseRepo resolves any host:owner/name or https://host/owner/name remote to an owner/name slug, so a GitLab or Bitbucket origin passes init's close-out guess and doctor's remote check, the run constructs a GitHub surface addressed at that slug, and the failure surfaces only at close-out time as 404s against api.github.com. forge.GitHub always addresses api.github.com (its API field is never set by pullRequestsForRun), so a non-github.com host is a remote the surface cannot speak with. A host check in ParseRepo (or at the three call sites that mean "GitHub remote": init's guess, doctor's check, pullRequestsForRun) would catch it where the operator can still fix it; GitHub Enterprise users would need forge.GitHub's API field wired first.
